accent-vibrant.note: Used as a raw fill only for the 6px status dot inside success badges (estado ACTIVO, contrato Vigente) -- the one deliberate exception to badges always using the desaturated -ink/-surface pair.

card-white.role: Fill of every card, table container, side-nav card and floating panel in the 2026-10-03 redesign; the canvas stays tinted (Bg) so a white card pops.

surface-hover-strong.note: Kept defined but currently unused: tables no longer use zebra striping (2026-10-03).

display.purpose: Page-level titles only (e.g. employee name on the profile page, module titles). Never marketing-hero scale.

headline.purpose: Section / tab-panel headers within a page.

title.purpose: Card headers, modal titles, table section headers.

body.purpose: Form field values, paragraph text, modal copy. WCAG floor -- never smaller than 1rem.

data.purpose: Dense table cells only (0.875rem) -- the one place text legitimately drops below Body size.

label.purpose: Table column headers (uppercase) and small captions / form-field and filter labels (sentence case) -- functional micro-label, not a decorative eyebrow.

mono.purpose: Copy-exactly values only (temporary passwords, codes). System monospace stack.

shadows.name: floating
shadows.purpose: Dropdowns, popovers, date pickers, info tooltips -- anything detached from normal page flow.

shadows.name: modal
shadows.purpose: Dialogs and the multi-step employee creation wizard.

zIndex.name: tooltip
zIndex.note: Top of the scale -- a tooltip must never be occluded by a modal, toast, or sticky nav open at the same time.

motion.name: ease-standard
motion.purpose: Default ease-out-quint for state transitions, hover/focus feedback, panel open/close.

motion.name: scroll-easing
motion.purpose: Wraps every independently-scrolling content pane so wheel/touch scroll eases continuously instead of stepping section-by-section. Native scrollTop under the hood (position: sticky stays compatible); sidebar nav and fixed chrome stay outside it; respects prefers-reduced-motion by default.

narrative.overview: HRMS aed is where a construction company keeps the truth about its people -- contracts, salaries, seguridad social, medical restrictions, disciplinary history. The system behaves like a well-kept ledger, not a marketing surface: every screen is built to be scanned fast, trusted completely, and never ambiguous. aed's own brand identity is bold, dynamic, and vibrant (a signature green-to-blue gradient, electric blue, bright green) -- this product wears that identity as a precise accent, not as a wash across dense data screens. Color earns its place; most of the interface is calm, cool-tinted neutral so that the two moments of real color -- a primary action, a status badge, the login/empty-state gradient -- read as deliberate, not decorative. The product rejects two failure modes equally: the outdated enterprise look (dense gray forms, unlabeled tables, generic icon sets) and the generic AI-SaaS look (identical cards, gradient hero metrics, uppercase eyebrows, side-stripe borders). It is also not a consumer app -- RR.HH. staff spend all day here, and every employee will occasionally self-serve their own profile, so the interface must flex between power-user density and lighter guided moments without changing its visual language. The 2026-10-03 redesign unified the whole product: one typeface (Inter), white cards on the tinted canvas, a dark Azul Profundo sidebar, a brand-gradient hero on every detail view, and tables that read like a list of people rather than a spreadsheet.
keyCharacteristics: Redesigned 2026-10-03: one typeface (Inter), white cards on the tinted canvas, dark Azul Profundo sidebar, brand-gradient hero on detail views, person-first tables
Cool, blue-tinted neutral canvas -- never the warm cream/sand AI default
Azul Vibrante and Verde Vibrante appear only as precise accents, never as large fills
Employee profile is the hub: sections, not scattered top-level CRUD screens -- underline tabs for short sets, sticky vertical nav past ~8 sections
Flat-by-default surfaces with tonal layering; shadows reserved for floating elements only
Responsive motion without choreography -- confidence through clarity, not spectacle
Every independently-scrolling pane eases its scroll via Lenis so long pages read as one continuous surface
Record-editing views open read-only; one global Editar control gates the whole page into edit mode at once

rules.name: The No-Cream Rule
rules.body: Off-white aed (#F0ECE6) is a warm print neutral from the brand manual -- right for business cards and letterhead, wrong for a screen. It never appears as the app canvas.

rules.name: The Rationed Brand Rule
rules.body: Azul Vibrante and Verde Vibrante combined should cover roughly 20% of any given screen's surface area (raised from 20% on 2026-10-01 to cover the Dashboard's KPI numbers/icons, chart data-ink, and card top accent line) -- still a budget, not a free-for-all: no colored fill behind an icon, no colored tile background.

rules.name: The Tabular Numerals Rule
rules.body: Any column of numbers (salarios, dias, cedulas, valores) uses font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums so digits align vertically. Since 2026-10-03 body sets it globally, so it is the default, not a per-column chore.

rules.name: The Floating-Only Rule
rules.body: If it doesn't detach from the page's normal flow, it doesn't get a shadow. Depth is earned by z-index, not applied by default.

rules.name: The Fluid Scroll Rule
rules.body: Every independently-scrolling content pane is wrapped in Lenis (root={false}) so scroll input eases into a continuous glide instead of stepping section by section. Native scrollTop under the hood keeps position: sticky compatible. Sidebar nav and fixed chrome stay outside it. Respects prefers-reduced-motion by default.

rules.name: The Full-Width Form Rule
rules.body: Forms take the full content width, organized into horizontal rows of fields grouped by named section -- never a single narrow vertical field stack.

rules.name: The View/Edit Mode Rule
rules.body: Record-editing views render read-only by default. One global Editar/Guardar/Cancelar control lives in the page header, never repeated per section -- driven by one shared boolean gating each section's fieldset disabled.

rules.name: The Explain-on-Demand Rule
rules.body: A dense dashboard's KPIs and charts get their explanation via an Info Tooltip next to the title (hover + keyboard focus, role=tooltip), not via permanent caption text under every tile -- permanent captions on every tile is the identical-card-grids AI-SaaS tell wearing a data-viz costume. Reserve a permanent caption for context that's load-bearing to read the chart correctly at a glance.

rules.name: The Back Link Rule
rules.body: Any route reached by drilling into one specific record (a real :id, not a :section tab selector) renders a BackLink (components/ui/BackLink.jsx) in its page header pointing to the list/parent it came from. The sidebar rail is never an acceptable substitute -- getting back that way means opening the category flyout and re-clicking the item, forcing the user to re-navigate the tree instead of retracing one step.

rules.name: The Persistent Filters Rule
rules.body: A list view's search box, filter selects, and current page are part of that screen's state -- leaving via BackLink/sidebar/browser-back and coming straight back must not reset them. Plain useState loses everything on remount; use usePersistentState (hooks/usePersistentState.js, same call signature as useState) which persists to sessionStorage under a page-namespaced key instead.

rules.name: The Topbar Trigger Rule
rules.body: Location and session/utility controls live in .topbar (a white 68px bar with a 2px aed-gradient bottom edge) inside <main>, never in the sidebar. Left: a breadcrumb 'Group > Screen' for staff (company/position block for employees). Right: notification bell and Accesos gear as identical 40px circles, a 1x28px divider, then the UserMenu 44px pill (34px gradient avatar + name + caret). Panels are white, radius-lg, floating shadow. The gear only shows for accounts with ver_usuarios, ver_roles or ADMIN.

rules.name: The Login Split Screen Rule
rules.body: LoginPage.jsx is a two-column split screen under a 5px aed-gradient top bar. Left: a brand panel (real photo under an Azul Profundo scrim, white-silhouette logo, headline, benefit chips; aria-hidden, hidden below 900px). Right: the Bg canvas with one centered white card (max 440px, radius 20px, brand-tinted shadow -- the one deliberate floating exception) holding the colored logo, a welcome title, 48px icon inputs with a password toggle, an error alert and a full-width 50px Azul Vibrante submit. Copy and photo are content; layout and contrast rules are mechanic. CambiarPasswordPage.jsx does not get this treatment.

rules.name: The Sortable Columns Rule
rules.body: Every data table column holding a comparable value (text, number, date) is clickable to sort: unsorted -> ascending -> descending -> unsorted, one column sorted at a time, clicking a different column resets to ascending on the new column. Always built from the same two pieces -- useSortableTable(rows, valueGetters) (hooks/useSortableTable.js) owns the sort state and comparison, SortHeader (components/ui/SortHeader.jsx) renders inside the existing <th> as label + arrow (arrow glyphs: ascending, descending, neutral -- 35% opacity at rest, full opacity + color-primary when active). Never a different icon set, never reimplemented per table.

rules.name: The Rationed KPI Rule
rules.body: A dashboard shows 5 KPI tiles at most, in one flat grid -- never grouped into multiple labeled sub-sections (the original dashboard had 10 tiles across 4 groups). Before adding a KPI it must clear two bars: not derivable from another KPI already on screen (Total/Activos/Retirados collapsed to just Activos), and not the same underlying query shown twice (Contratos por vencer + Proximos retiros were literally the same query -- merged; Personas en vacaciones + incapacidades merged into one Ausentes hoy tile). A KPI that is really a reminder/list (birthdays this month) is an Alert (the neutral-severity group in the Alerts panel), never a KPI tile.

rules.name: The ApexCharts Rule
rules.body: All dashboard charts use ApexCharts (react-apexcharts) -- never Recharts, never any other charting library. Pick the chart shape from what the data asks, not from habit -- a first pass that mechanically re-skinned every chart as a bar produced six same-ish boxes, the identical-cards tell wearing bars instead of icons. Four shapes: category bar (horizontal, single DATA_INK color, for a category list that can grow long -- Departamento); donut (DonutChart.jsx, CATEGORICAL_RAMP colors assigned in first-seen order, Sin especificar/Sin asignar always NEUTRAL_SLICE gray never a ramp color via esSinDato(), center shows the total, legend at right -- for a composition question with 2-6 nominal categories, Genero/Tipo de contrato); ordinal bar (vertical, ORDINAL_RAMP, plotOptions.bar.distributed:true -- for ORDERED buckets where sequence is the point, Antiguedad/Distribucion salarial, never a donut, a donuts clock-position order is weaker than a bars left-to-right); trend line (stroke.curve:smooth, no area fill). ChartCard wrapper (title + InfoTooltip + .srOnly summary, never role=img) and usePrefersReducedMotion() -> chart.animations.enabled stay unchanged under any shape.

rules.name: The Alerts Panel Rule
rules.body: Dashboard alerts are ONE Surface panel (AlertGroup.jsx, .alertsPanel) with 2-3 severity groups stacked inside, hairline-divided (.alertGroup + .alertGroup border-top, never a colored side border) -- never a grid of same-size cards, one per data source (six identical AlertCard boxes before, two of which -- Licencias vencidas + Certificaciones vencidas -- silently queried overlapping data and showed the same row twice). Groups: Requiere atencion (danger, already-past-date items merged from every source into one deduplicated list, each row tagged with its real tipo), Por vencer (warning, not-yet-due-but-needs-action), a neutral group for anything that is a reminder not a risk (birthdays). Rows sort most-urgent-first within a group. Each row: a fixed-min-width Label-typography tag (columns line up like a table), title+meta, and a right-aligned tabular-nums days indicator (danger-ink + weight 600 only inside the danger group). An empty group still shows its header (0 count) plus a one-line empty message, never disappears silently.

rules.name: The Accesos Rule
rules.body: Account/access administration (who has a login, what role) is a normal route styled exactly like the employee profile (sticky vertical nav beside content), never a floating drawer/modal -- a slide-out overlay version of this was built and explicitly rejected by the user for not feeling like a normal part of the app. AccesosLayout.jsx (features/configuracion/) is the shared wrapper, same structure as WizardLayout.jsx mode=edit (reuses WizardLayout.module.css directly): a vertical nav (.nav/.navItem/.navItemActive) beside .content, one item per Accesos section. Usuarios y perfiles is the reference real section; Roles y permisos/Parametros/Importadores are documented enDesarrollo placeholders in the same nav. Every real page under Accesos wraps its own content in AccesosLayout individually -- no single shared container page, exactly like no single page wraps every employee profile tab. The topbar keeps a gear icon (Settings, lucide-react, same 44px/radius-md as every topbar trigger) between NotificationBell and UserMenu, but it is a plain navigation Link to /usuarios, not a stateful trigger -- a real URL, back/forward and bookmarks all work like any other route. Two concrete pitfalls found and fixed: (1) WizardLayout.module.css .content (shared with the employee profile) has no gap since it only ever wraps one .card there -- an Accesos page puts multiple siblings inside <AccesosLayout> (toolbar, error banner, table/card), so AccesosLayout.jsx wraps children in its own local .contentInner (flex column, gap: var(--space-lg), in AccesosLayout.module.css) instead of adding gap to the shared file. (2) never cap an Accesos card/form with a max-width (e.g. 720px) -- the Full-Width Rule applies here same as everywhere else, and a capped width is exactly what makes a .row of side-by-side fields (Nombre + Email) wrap into a vertical stack instead of staying horizontal. Third pitfall: .row never sets align-items -- stretch (the default) is what keeps a rows inputs aligned regardless of which Field has helper/error text and which does not, since Field is flex-direction column and none of its children are flex-grown (extra stretch height lands after the shorter fields own content, not before the input). Adding align-items: flex-end to .row ties every controls position to the bottom of the tallest item including trailing helper text -- a bare non-Field control (a Button with no Field around it, e.g. Generar contrasena aleatoria) then drifts to chase that. Fix: give a bare control next to a Field its own label-height spacer (visibility: hidden, --text-label-size, line-height 1.3, matching Fields own .label metrics) so it starts level with the neighboring input -- see .actionRow/.actionRowSpacer in Usuarios.module.css. Updated 2026-10-03: the menu is its own white 248px card with grouped sections (Accesos: Usuarios, Roles; Sistema: Datos), each row an icon chip + label + one-line hint; the content pane carries min-width: 0 so wide tables cannot push the page.

rules.name: The One-to-Many Selection Rule
rules.body: Any field assigning multiple items (a permission matrix, a multi-role picker, users assigned to a record, workflow approvers) uses CheckboxGroup.jsx (short fixed set of booleans, Surface Sunken auto-fill grid, no search needed) or CheckboxListSelect.jsx (long/growing/groupable list -- selected items as removable chips above a bordered searchable panel, real production usage: Gerencias/Procesos/Frentes in WizardLaboralStep.jsx) -- never a bare native <select multiple> (Ctrl/Cmd+click is not discoverable, no search, no compact view of the selection) and never an unstyled run-on paragraph of checkboxes wrapping by screen width. This closes a real gap found in a sibling aed project. CheckboxListSelect's checkbox list starts collapsed (2026-09-03, ported from Contratacion/ex-Indirectos where this originates) -- opens on focus/click of the search input (role=combobox, aria-expanded), closes on outside click or Escape; the open list scrolls internally (max-height 280px, overflow-y auto, overscroll-behavior: contain, data-lenis-prevent so Lenis doesn't hijack the wheel over it).

rules.name: The Pagination Rule
rules.body: Every server-paginated table uses Pagination.jsx (components/ui/) -- same footer bar, same two buttons ("‹ Anterior" / "Siguiente ›"), same "Mostrando X-Y de Z" + "Pagina X de Y" wording in every project. Never a hand-rolled pager, never numbered page buttons with ellipsis. Self-hides when total===0 or a single page -- callers never guard for that themselves. <Pagination page={meta.page} pageSize={meta.pageSize} total={meta.total} onPageChange={setPage} />.

rules.name: The Fluid Width Rule
rules.body: No page, card, or section gets a hardcoded max-width that caps it below the available viewport -- a view adapts to however wide the screen is, never assumes a fixed width and lets content wrap/cut off around that assumption. Real bugs fixed on this: Usuarios form card at max-width:720px (field rows wrapped vertically when they fit fine full-width) and MiPerfilPage.page at max-width:900px (a self-service page still gets no width cap -- lighter/guided means fewer fields, not a narrower viewport). Legitimate max-width only on content narrow by nature (search box, filter dropdown, tooltip bubble, login split-screen text column, a 75ch prose paragraph) -- never on a .page/.card/container wrapping a table or a form .row. Content wider than any viewport (a many-column table) scrolls horizontally inside its own container (overflow-x: auto on the wrapper), never clipped, never forcing the whole page to scroll sideways.

rules.name: The Row Icon Actions Rule
rules.body: Every table/list row's Editar and Activar/Inactivar actions render as icon buttons (EditIconButton/ToggleActivoIconButton, components/ui/RowIconButtons.jsx), never as text buttons reading "Editar"/"Inactivar"/"Activar" -- pencil icon for Editar, circle+line (inactivar, turns danger-red on hover) or circle+cross (activar) for the toggle, 32x32px, in a flex .actionsCell aligned right. One shared component, not copy-pasted SVG per table -- before this rule, Empresas/Usuarios/Empleados each duplicated the same markup by hand while CatalogCrudTab.jsx (the generic table behind Gerencias/Procesos/Cargos/Centros de Costo/Area Contable/Proyectos/Etapas/Frentes -- 8 tables from one file) and two inline lists (CargoDetailPage.jsx funciones, EmpresaEditPage.jsx jornadas) still had literal "Editar"/"Inactivar" text buttons. A page-level edit-mode toggle (the big "Editar"/"Guardar"/"Cancelar" button pair at the top of a detail page, e.g. EmpresaEditPage.jsx/CargoDetailPage.jsx/the employee profile's WizardLayout.jsx) is a different pattern (see The View/Edit Mode Rule) and stays text -- this rule is only for per-row actions inside a table or list.

rules.name: The One Family Rule
rules.body: The product uses a single typeface, Inter (variable, self-hosted via @fontsource-variable/inter). Never add a second family for 'personality'; vary weight and size. The only other family is --font-mono, for copy-exactly values (temporary passwords, codes).

rules.name: The Tracking Rule
rules.body: Inter is tracked by size: -0.006em on body/data text (set on body), -0.012em on h1-h4, +0.03em only on uppercase Label text. No per-page letter-spacing.

rules.name: The Table Rule
rules.body: Tables are white cards (radius-lg, 1px Border) with a quiet Label-type header, no zebra, no colored header underline, Surface Sunken row hover, a person cell (36px initials avatar + name + document/email), Badges for status, an em dash in Ink Muted for empty values, tabular/nowrap dates and numbers, single-line ellipsis for long text. Rows that open a record are clickable; Reportes tables are read-only on purpose. A table must fit at 1440px without the sticky actions column covering the previous one; a flex parent needs min-width: 0.

rules.name: The Detail Hero Rule
rules.body: Every detail view opens with the Detail Hero (Azul Profundo to Azul Vibrante gradient, 72px avatar, name, one subtitle, status badges), followed by a KPI row or Section Cards. One hero per page, never repeated inside tabs.

rules.name: The Section Cards Rule
rules.body: Detail/edit forms are a vertical stack of named white cards (Title + one-line hint + fields) above an action bar: Cancelar left, primary right, a danger button for a destructive action only when allowed. System items show an Info banner instead of controls that do nothing.

rules.name: The Aligned Cards Rule
rules.body: Cards in a grid whose parts must line up use grid-row: span N with subgrid so each band takes the tallest sibling's height. Never clip text (no line-clamp, no fixed heights); reserve min-height for bands, and give transient messages their own band.

rules.name: The Detail Is a Route Rule
rules.body: A drill-down (a gerencia from the Organigrama) is its own route with a BackLink, a hero, KPIs and paginated lists. Modals are only for confirmations and one-time results (e.g. temporary passwords with a CSV download).

rules.name: The Notification Panel Rule
rules.body: The bell opens a 392px white panel: header with count chip and 'Marcar todas', tabs Todas / Sin leer / Contratos, a scrolling body (Por decidir, Tus solicitudes, contract reminders grouped by urgency with danger/warning/neutral chips) between a fixed header and a fixed footer link; empty state 'Estas al dia'. The badge counts pending decisions + unread + reminders.

dos: Do keep the app canvas cool-tinted neutral (#EDEEFE family) -- never the warm cream/sand AI default.
Do reserve Azul Vibrante and Verde Vibrante for actions, status, and identity moments.
Do use underline tabs for short section sets and a sticky vertical nav once a detail view outgrows a tab row -- the employee profile is the reference case at 21 sections.
Do use tabular-nums on every numeric table column.
Do give every loading/empty/error state real, deliberate content.
Do let list/table views and forms use the full content width, with form fields grouped into horizontal rows by named section.
Do gate an existing record's fields behind one global Editar/Guardar/Cancelar control in the page header.
Do wrap every independently-scrolling content pane in Lenis so scrolling eases continuously.
Do explain a non-obvious KPI or chart with an Info Tooltip next to its title instead of a permanent caption under every tile.
Do render a BackLink in the header of every route that drills into one specific record -- never leave the sidebar as the only way out of a screen.
Do keep a list view's search/filter/page state in usePersistentState, not useState -- it must survive leaving the screen and coming back.
Do keep every topbar trigger button consistent (40px circular icon triggers, 44px user pill) -- a mismatched-height row of buttons is the tell of an unplanned shell.

Do give the login screen a representative photo brand panel under an Azul Profundo scrim (never plain, uncovered) with the logo rendered as a white silhouette, and a single white form card (colored logo, welcome title, icon inputs) on the Bg canvas.
Do make every sortable data table column use useSortableTable + SortHeader, with the same ▲/▼/⇅ arrow and 3-click (asc/desc/none) cycle in every table.
Do keep a dashboard to 5 KPI tiles at most, in one flat grid, each one a metric nothing else on screen already implies.

Do build every dashboard chart with ApexCharts (react-apexcharts), and pick its shape (bar/donut/line) from what the data asks -- composition with few categories gets a donut, ordered buckets stay a bar, a trend stays a line.
Do group dashboard alerts into one Surface panel with 2-3 severity sections inside, hairline-divided -- never a grid of same-size boxes, one per data source.

Do put account/access administration behind a topbar gear icon that navigates to a normal route styled like the employee profile (sticky vertical nav, AccesosLayout.jsx) -- see the Accesos Rule -- never a floating drawer or modal, and never a category in the primary sidebar.

Do use CheckboxGroup.jsx (short fixed set) or CheckboxListSelect.jsx (long/searchable/groupable set) for any one-to-many assignment field -- see the One-to-Many Selection Rule -- never a native <select multiple> or an unstyled checkbox paragraph.
Do use Pagination.jsx for every server-paginated table -- same buttons/wording everywhere, self-hides when there is nothing to paginate (see the Pagination Rule).

Do let every page/card/section size itself to the actual viewport -- max-width only on content narrow by nature (search box, dropdown, tooltip, login text column, a prose paragraph), never on a page or a form/table wrapper (see the Fluid Width Rule).
Do use a single typeface (Inter) and vary weight/size for hierarchy; monospace only for copy-exactly values.
Do open every detail view with the Detail Hero and build detail/edit forms as a stack of Section Cards.
Do keep a drill-down as its own route; use a Modal only to confirm an action or reveal a one-time result.
Do align cards in a grid with subgrid and min-height bands -- never by clipping their text.
donts: Don't replicate the SAP/Oracle-2000s look: dense gray forms, mismatched icon styles/weights thrown together ad hoc, unlabeled cramped tables (this doesn't ban lucide-react itself -- the sidebar rail uses it deliberately, one library/size/stroke weight, applied consistently).
Don't ship generic AI-SaaS scaffolding: identical cards, gradient hero metrics, uppercase eyebrows, side-stripe borders.
Don't let the interface feel like a playful consumer app.
Don't use Off-white aed (#F0ECE6) as a screen background.
Don't add a shadow to anything that isn't floating above the page.
Don't apply gradient-text anywhere -- the aed gradient is a graphic accent element, never a text treatment.
Don't repeat an Editar/Guardar/Cancelar control inside every tab or section of a detail view -- one global control per page.
Don't grow the accent-vibrant status dot into a stripe, larger chip, or full badge fill -- it stays a 6px indicator.
Don't ship a drill-down route (a real :id, not a :section tab) without a BackLink in its header -- making the sidebar the only way back is the failure this rule exists to prevent.
Don't hold a list view's filters/search/page in plain useState -- it silently resets the moment the user leaves the screen and comes back.
Don't put session controls (logout, who am I) in the sidebar -- that's the topbar's job, a sidebar footer duplicating UserMenu is duplicated UI, not helpful redundancy.
Don't place a login-form field inside a bordered/shadowed card anymore -- LoginPage's form sits open on the panel, wide (480px), no box.

Don't show the colored aed logo on a dark surface (the login photo panel, the sidebar) -- render it as a white silhouette (filter: brightness(0) invert(1)); the white form card is where the colored logo appears.
Don't ship a data table with a fixed, unsortable row order, and don't build a one-off sort implementation with different arrows/behavior -- reuse SortHeader + useSortableTable.
Don't add a KPI tile that's derivable from another tile already on screen, or that's the same query as another tile framed differently -- merge or cut it.
Don't use Recharts (or any charting library besides ApexCharts) for a new chart.
Don't default every chart to a bar just because the last one was a bar -- a composition question with few categories wants a donut, not another bar.
Don't render dashboard alerts as a grid of same-size cards, one per data source -- group by severity into one panel instead.

Don't implement account/access administration as a floating drawer, panel, or modal, and don't add it as a category in the primary left sidebar either -- it is a normal route with its own vertical nav (AccesosLayout.jsx), reached from a topbar gear icon that is a plain link (see the Accesos Rule).

Don't implement a multi-item assignment field as a bare <select multiple> or as an unstyled, wrapping paragraph of checkboxes -- use CheckboxGroup.jsx or CheckboxListSelect.jsx depending on list size (see the One-to-Many Selection Rule).
Don't hand-roll a pagination footer per page, or use numbered page buttons with ellipsis -- use Pagination.jsx (see the Pagination Rule).

Don't cap a page, card, or table/form wrapper with a fixed max-width -- it makes rows wrap into a vertical stack that would fit fine at full width, and no view should assume a fixed screen size (see the Fluid Width Rule).
Don't add zebra striping, a sunken header or a colored header underline to a table.
Don't make report rows clickable or add a second typeface.
Don't clip or truncate a card's text (line-clamp, fixed heights) to make cards line up.
